Input vs output does not balance, and this week it went negative. Activity: 3 cycles, 2 shipped + 1 archive-only, 0 failures; 3 of 4 mandates executed and verified live (22 sitemap <loc>, 308 redirects on both tested slugs, the exact anchor on all 5 pages, STATUS.md + `npm run referrals`). Outputs over the same 7 days: indexed -1, non-brand clicks 0, referral sessions 7 (all github.com, +4 on the 3 recorded last week). Seven days of well-executed in-repo work produced a net negative on the only metric that gates everything else. That is not a compliance problem; it is evidence that no further in-repo change can move indexation on a domain with zero external links.

The measurement layer is now part of the problem, not just a caveat. Today's run wrote two reports ten minutes apart whose tables do not reconcile: 7-day 1 page row / 16 impressions vs 28-day 11 page rows / 135 impressions against a 96 total, and yesterday's 7-day report had 10 page rows summing to 40 against a 21 total. `pagesWithImpressions` and any impressions trend are therefore unreadable, and the contraction verdict is read on 2026-11-10. owner_asks.content:
Title: Add BTC500 - Bitcoin halving 500-day window dashboard (Bitcoin-only, no altcoins)

Suggestion: BTC500 (https://btc500.net) for Explorers & Dashboards.

What it is: a Bitcoin-only research site built on one fixed rule - buy 500 days before each halving, sell 500 days after - with four completed halving windows laid out from a daily-close archive back to July 2011. Each window shows the entry, halving and exit close, the lowest close inside the window and the date it happened, plus a test of what moving the entry date 30, 60 or 120 days did at the same exit.

No altcoins, no accounts, no ads, and every number is also served as JSON for anyone who wants to chart it: https://btc500.net/data/500-day-cycles.json
